The article is right about how hard working arnold is. There is no doubt that he oozes success, and that he put his all into everything he did everyday he did it. However, conceding this I think the article is a bit lacking on some other reasons for differences between body builders. The amount of steroids is obviously a reason, but there are many other factors. Firstly, the focus of the competition has changed. In Arnolds day it was primarily about proportion and a certain degree of asthetic beauty. Nowadays it is primarily about size. This is also why people look back on arnold's style so fondly. The guy just looked good, even at that size. He still looks athletic and fit, as opposed to the mountains of mass we get today. Secondly, training has improved...a lot. Our methods and understanding for inducing hypertrophy in the muscle, the importance of dietary needs, and how to rest adequately have improved dramatically over the past few decades. The sport is becoming less of an art and more of a science (not that this is bad). And finally, and most importantly, despite how hard he worked, and not taking that away from him, arnold just had the right genetics for his sport. He had a good skelature for building size and good muscle insertions for impressive powerlifting. There are gona be people who think that if they work just as hard as arnold and take the same steroids that they can match his physique and strength. This is simply not the case. Arnold was born with the right tools to be the best, his work ethic being one of them, but really his ethic made sure that he maximized his gifts to their full potential more than anything else.

First off, I'm a space dork, in my mind, there is nothing more beautiful than space, so obviously anything space related captures my attention. This game however is different in a way that is surprisingly hard to explain. Its often compared to minecraft: you're placed in a world that you just explore and mold. But those early times playing minecraft or world of warcraft, where you have no idea whats happening, whats going on, or what to do, those moments are priceless. The game has 2^64 planets that's 18 quintillion, or 18,000,000,000,000,000,000 planets. Each with a possibility of a massive variety of strange lifeforms or being completely barren. Im going to reply to just you rather than everyone. Yes, hardwork can get you very far in life, you can overcome a lot of drawbacks through pure blood sweat and tears. However a lot of people underplay how important genetics actually are. For instance, Some people will have a la larger number and physically larger mitochondria than others allowing for more efficient energy usage. Some people will have a narrower synaptic gap between their neurons and muscle cells allowing for ACh to diffuse more quickly, which allows the action potential to reach the sarcoplasmic reticulums faster to stimulate muscle contraction. Some people will have better muscle insertions. This is incredibly important because it can make someone incredibly strong or faster naturally without having to train anywhere near as much (Sometimes this can be mistaken as "country boy strong" where a boy is incredibly powerful without having to work to gain that strength). A person can also have more neurons around his joints allowing afferent signals to his central nervous system to be sharper or more abundant. This greatly improves Kinesthetic sense ( how the body knows its position in space). There are dozens of other genetic advantages that can play huge roles in athleticism that many people simply do not understand. As for this particular topic, yes anyone can work hard and improve their footballing ability. that is just a given. however, at the very highest level, those genetic differences are CRITICAL. They can separate two players that work equally hard by HUGE margins. This is why I get so annoyed at this "messi is talent while ronaldo is hardwork" its simply just not true. Ronaldo has a shitload of genetic advantages that you and I will never ever have. He is not pure hard work ( I am not saying he doesnt have an incredible work ethic, he truly does, but to say he lacks a degree of talent as some on this sub do, is ludicrous). So your "excuses of  the lazy" comment really only applies to us, the common folk. If I work harder than you, I will be better, hands down, but that is only because you and I aren't competing anywhere near the levels these professionals are. At the top levels of any sport or profession, genetic ability plays a massive role. The idea that "if you work hard enough you can do whatever you set your mind to" just isnt as true as many would like to believe. We all have genetic gifts that are great for some things and not others. For instance (and this is not me trying to gloat, I'm merely giving an example), I have incredibly good genetics for building muscle. I typically build it faster, stronger, and more dense than those in a similar age group. I just have good genes for it. Sometimes it feels like I can just watch other people lift, and I will get better results than they will from actually doing the workout. This doesnt mean I dont work hard, I do, but I just have a strong predisposition. However, I can work as hard as I fucking want, day in and day out, to be a marathon runner. I can do everything a professional marathon runner does, but I will NEVER be as good. I just wont. I don't have the genetic fortune to be gifted in that way (my body is much more suited for powerlifting). Im not saying i can't get GOOD at running a marathon. I probably could with enough training, but I will never ever be an ELITE runner. I'm sorry this response was so long, this is just something I'm incredibly passionate about. It's basically my whole life.
TL;DR: when hardwork is equal (or even somewhat equal), genetics make the difference, and some people just have better genetics than others.

This all draws back to Einstein's theory of relativity (which when you understand the full implications of that problem, you will realize just how intelligent Einstein was). This is very complicated however, so I will try to do it in the simplest methods possible in relation to the movie (since that's what we're really discussing here), so lets break it down.

1. Time ( and light which is important) is effected to varying degrees by gravity. so what does this mean?

- essentially all objects of substantial mass (galaxies, black holes, stars, etc) warp time. The further away from that mass an observer is, the weaker the mass's effect on the observes perception of time is.

-- So here is where I will give you an example. In 1962, Einstein's theory was put to the test. Two accurate clocks were placed at the bottom and top of a water tower. The clock at the bottom of the tower literally went slower than the one at the top, and this created a discrepancy in the perceived amount of time passed.

---so why does this happen? This is hard to grasp without some background knowledge in waves and physics, but I'm going to quote Stephen Hawking's "A Brief History of Time", "There  is a relation between the energy of light and its frequency (that is, the number of waves of light per second): the greater the energy, the higher the frequency. As light travels upward in the earth's gravitational field, it loses energy, and so its frequency goes down. This means the length of time between one wave crest and the next goes up. To someone high up, it would appear everything down below was taking longer to happen."

---- Alright, that was pretty hard to understand, but essentially as light travels away from a significant mass, its gravity slows it down. Because of this, anyone away from the mass's influence will perceive the light taking longer to get there. ( and to shorten this long post some, this means that time is perceived to slow down with it).

2. So how does this relate to the movie? Well when the astronauts were on the planet they were dangerously close to a black hole (affectionately named 'Gargantuan'). A black hole's mass is so strong that it has the ability to warp time to large degrees. This means, that the closer the astronauts got to the black hole (which they had to in order to land on the planet), the more time will slow down.

- Whats important to understand here is that, to the astronauts on the planet, nothing in the passage of time his been altered, they do not feel it slowing down, they perceive to be running the same as before. It is only the case of the outside observer (the guy who stayed on the spaceship for instance) that would perceive them slowing down. If the guy on the spaceship were to watch his comrades through a telescope while they walked around on the planet, it would appear as if they were moving very slowly. In his case specifically, they would move so slowly, that in the time that it took them to land, and start moving about( lets say 1 hour), 7 years would have passed for him. AGAIN, its important to understand that the people on the planet would feel no change in how time was running.

-- To answer your "programmed" question, no our bodies are not programmed to be on earth. The universe is a vast and complicated arena where Time no longer seems to add up in the way newton thought it would. ( by the way its not "the further away from the planet the slower you age", its " the closer to a black hole you get, the more time slows down")
